A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OBS-Diff research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, generation-quality measurements, timing results, ablations, and qualitative outputs in Section 5 and Appendices C-D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SDXL/EcoDiff comparisons and robustness experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The timestep-weighted Hessian, module-package calibration, OBS updates, sparsity extensions, and reciprocal-rank fusion procedure remain unchanged. The added SDXL evaluation does not document a new algorithmic component or adaptation.

E1.justification: The represented coverage remains text-to-image generation using GCC3M/MS-COCO and CIFAR-10 DDPM evaluation. SDXL, alternative inference settings, and MS-COCO training-split calibration add model configurations and protocol controls within this coverage, rather than new tasks or data domains.

E2.justification: EcoDiff moves from related-work discussion in v1 to an evaluated structured-pruning comparator on SD3.5-Large and SDXL in v2 Tables 3-4. This substantially strengthens the comparator set beyond v1's L1-norm-only large-model structured comparisons; the other baseline sets remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds structured evaluation of the 2.57B SDXL model at 15%, 20%, and 30% sparsity. Appendix D adds fixed-checkpoint tests across CFG scales, sampling-step counts, and solvers on a 1K MS-COCO subset, plus an MS-COCO-versus-GCC3M calibration control evaluated on 5K prompts. These are additional experimental designs; existing main evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests sensitivity to guidance strength, sampling steps, solver choice, and calibration-data source, addressing whether pruning generalizes beyond its calibration conditions. The earlier timestep-weighting, module-package, and calibration-size ablations remain. One qualitative structured-pruning example, v1 Figure 12, is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Tables 3-4 and 11-14, including SDXL at 30% sparsity: FID 29.75 for OBS-Diff versus 101.96 for EcoDiff. Existing main scores remain unchanged. The dense SD3-Medium reference in v1 Table 8/v2 Table 9 changes from FID/CLIP/ImageReward 31.59/0.3156/0.7549 to 36.14/0.3162/0.9029, matching Table 1; its pruned rows are unchanged. The cherry-blossom qualitative comparison in v1 Figure 12 is omitted.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(8), their mathematical definitions, and their derivations are unchanged. Appendix D's assertions about ODE preservation and generalization are empirical interpretations, without new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free one-shot pruning, timestep-aware Hessians, efficient module packages, multiple sparsity granularities, and state-of-the-art performance. New experiments support this retained contribution scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D introduces substantive interpretations about preserved semantic capability, ODE-trajectory integrity, solver independence, and absence of calibration overfitting. Some exceed the evidence: Table 13 preserves the best SD v2.1 sampler but changes the remaining ranking, while Table 14's calibration-source comparison cannot definitively prove non-overfitting. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents calibration settings for the robustness experiments, including CFG 7.0, 25 steps, and Euler for SD3-Medium, and PNDM for SD v2.1. It also specifies the calibration-source control's splits. Appendix B's hardware and common configurations, and the code-access information, remain unchanged; EcoDiff-specific implementation and budget details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang and Wang (2025) on faster Stable Diffusion and removes five general pruning references, including DepGraph, Deep Compression, and Is Oracle Pruning the True Oracle? EcoDiff receives direct comparative positioning in Section 5.4, while the broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally edits the introduction and structured-results discussion, adds a short methodology overview, and inserts a robustness appendix before the qualitative appendix, now labeled E. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the SDXL comparison table and four robustness tables, and expands the retained SD3.5-Large table with EcoDiff rows. These substantially extend the displayed evidence. Existing plots and qualitative panels are redistributed across pages, and v1 Figure 12 is removed; the framework diagram and overall visual style remain.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through a diffusion-specific structured baseline and controlled robustness tests, and corrects the inconsistent dense SD3-Medium reference. The gain is tempered by missing EcoDiff implementation details and overinterpretation in Appendix D, including the unsupported full-ranking preservation and definitive non-overfitting assertions. The added evidence remains useful, but these limitations prevent a substantial overall quality improvement.
